clue.text: Thick fences top a fine old naval base

indicators.note: to fence something is to enclose it, so the word for thick surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: thick in the sense of dim-witted means slow
a cap is a top or lid
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A dim official surrounds the old naval base with a fence to cap it off.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAPA FLOW in Orkney was the Royal Navy's main anchorage in both world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa Flow was the chief British fleet anchorage in two world wars, a historic naval base.

clue.text: Character going to extremes in Sophocles

definitions.text: Character going to extremes in Sophocles

parts.words: Character going to extremes in Sophocles
parts.note: the Greek letter that the playwright's name, written in Greek, begins and ends with: the letter standing at both extremes of the word

explanation.surface: A figure in a Greek tragedy pushes everything to the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a letter, not a person in a play; in Greek the name Sophocles both starts and ends with the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the Greek letter for S, the character found at either end of the dramatist's name.

clue.text: Article transposed suggested solution in Cluedo mystery

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a Cluedo accusation runs 'Miss Scarlet in the study'; swapping the two nouns round gives study in Scarlet

explanation.surface: In a game of Cluedo, someone offers a guess at whodunnit after shuffling an item.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo is the board game where players name a suspect and a room; 'Scarlet in the study' with its two nouns transposed becomes the title of the first Sherlock Holmes novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Study in Scarlet is Conan Doyle's first Sherlock Holmes story, a detective mystery.

clue.text: Make known girl's put on a little weight

indicators.note: one piece is put on, that is placed next to, the other in the charade

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's is 'has' and joins it
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A girl reports that she has gained a bit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to declare publicly, to make something known.

clue.text: Liberal remains after firing whip

parts.note: ash is what is left after something is burnt

explanation.surface: A Liberal stays on after being sacked, and the party whip cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing' suggests dismissal, but it is burning, which leaves ash.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash is a whip, or a stroke with one.

clue.text: Come round, in more than one sense creating alarm

parts.note: to come round after sleep or a faint is to wake up
in a second sense, to come round to someone's house is to call

explanation.surface: Regaining consciousness, in more ways than one, sets off a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In more than one sense' tells you to read 'Come round' twice: once as reviving, once as paying a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake-up call is a ring that rouses a sleeper, so it serves as an alarm.

clue.text: Vice Chancellor with a book containing old word list

indicators.note: containing means the letters for old go inside the others

parts.note: VC is the abbreviation for Vice Chancellor

explanation.surface: A university head carries an old book of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocab, short for vocabulary, is a list of words being learnt.

clue.text: Duty on petrol, say, with third off? I'd fill the tank!

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a duty

indicators.note: the third letter of the word for petrol is removed

parts.note: petrol is an example of fuel

explanation.surface: With a duty on petrol and a third off the price, a motorist would fill up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: a vatful is the amount that would fill the tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A vatful is the contents of a full vat, which is a large tank.

clue.text: Suffering inertia, the class daydreams

indicators.note: a suffering thing is in a bad state, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A lethargic class sits gazing out of the window.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in the air are fanciful plans or hopes that will never be realised, much like daydreams.

clue.text: Waitress suggesting cake, perhaps, hands round grand one

parts.note: bunny read as bun-ny, like a bun, which is an example of a cake
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: turned round, so the two hands appear in the other order

parts.note: L and R are the left and right hands

explanation.surface: A waitress offers cake and passes it round to an important guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands round' reads as passing food about, but means left and right turned round; a bunny girl is a Playboy-club waitress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunny girl is a nightclub waitress in a costume with rabbit ears and a tail.

clue.text: To take a person's fish, boy you've got to be quick!

parts.note: to take is to get
one's means a person's
a skate is a flat fish
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An angler steals someone's catch and tells the lad to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Get one's skates on is an idiom urging someone to hurry up.

clue.text: Heat can make a run grim

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
dour means grim or stern

explanation.surface: Hot weather can turn a jog into an ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' reads as weather but means passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate warmth of feeling, heat in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Corporation backing partner's held acceptable for both parties

indicators.note: the letter for acceptable is held between the other pieces
backing means the word for corporation is read backwards

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum
an ally is a partner; the 's is 'has', joining it to the next word
U stands for upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A company backs a partner who has kept everything acceptable to both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business but is a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutually means jointly or reciprocally, applying to both parties at once.

clue.text: An outburst disrupted parade ground manoeuvres

indicators.note: the words are thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry shout breaks up the drill on the parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: About-turns are drill movements in which soldiers turn to face the opposite way.

clue.text: Stick with rugby player going through ups and downs

parts.note: a switch is a thin flexible stick
a back is a rugby player behind the scrum

explanation.surface: Armed with a stick, a rugby player has a run of good and bad fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: A switchback is a road or railway rising and falling steeply in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a route of repeated steep rises and falls, a series of ups and downs.

clue.text: Rogue that is entirely unknown to comedian

parts.note: sc., short for scilicet, means that is or namely
all means entirely
Y is an algebraic unknown
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: A rogue's nature is a total mystery to the comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous rascal, a rogue.

clue.text: Italian product needs a brief whisk

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to whisk is to stir

explanation.surface: An Italian product needs only a quick whisk.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling wine made in Piedmont, an Italian product.

clue.text: Readily agreed to fix touring car that's overturned

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the word for fix encloses the next piece

parts.note: to embed is to fix firmly

indicators.note: overturned means the word car is written backwards

explanation.surface: A mechanic sets about repairing a touring car that has rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' looks like a kind of car, but it means going round; 'that's overturned' turns the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or offer is to accept it readily and gladly.

clue.text: Do like to go around start of summer recess

indicators.note: the word for imitate goes around the letter that follows

parts.note: to ape is to copy, to do like someone

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of summer is taken

explanation.surface: Copy what others do at the start of the summer break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' suggests a holiday but is an architectural alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, typically at the east end of a church.

clue.text: In a bill, sum for arranging sort of advertisement

indicators.note: arranging means putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An advertiser works out the total to be shown on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Subliminal advertising works below the threshold of conscious perception.

clue.text: Heavenly radiator when filling a couple of pints short

indicators.note: filling means the word for when goes inside the other piece
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a quart is two pints
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A drinker feels a warm glow when served two pints that are under measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radiator' suggests a heater; here it is a body that radiates energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A quasar is a remote celestial object emitting vast amounts of energy, so a heavenly radiator.

clue.text: To prepare for a party hire out old houses

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the first pieces enclose the others

parts.note: to let is to hire out
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a celebration, someone rents out old homes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead up to something is to prepare the way for it gradually.

clue.text: Composer very nearly a god

indicators.note: the last letter of the composer is left off

parts.note: Johannes Brahms was a German composer

explanation.surface: A composer is regarded almost as a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahma is the Hindu creator god.

clue.text: Loudspeaker turned up concealed bug

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a PA, public address system, is a loudspeaker
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker turned up full hides a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests a hidden microphone; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect, a bug.

clue.text: Seize bus's occupants and steer

indicators.note: occupants are inside, so the letters are found within the words

explanation.surface: A hijacker grabs the bus and its passengers and takes the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' looks like a verb; it is a young ox.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebu is a humped ox, and a steer is a castrated male ox.

clue.text: Financial disaster to impact on West all the way

indicators.note: on means the word for impact comes after the others

parts.note: a street is a way
to crash is to collide

explanation.surface: A financial collapse hits the West from end to end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wall Street Crash of 1929 began the Great Depression.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wall Street Crash was the 1929 stock-market collapse, a notorious financial disaster.

clue.text: Odd traces of giant boar one snaps in America

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the words are traced out

explanation.surface: Faint tracks of a huge wild pig are found.
explanation.walkthrough: Gator is American shorthand for alligator.
explanation.definitionFit: A gator, an alligator, snaps its jaws and is found in the southern United States.

clue.text: Did shake obtained from milk container spill all round?

indicators.note: the word for spill goes all round the other piece

parts.note: to shed is to spill or let fall
an udder holds a cow's milk

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer trembled when milk spilled out of the pail.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuddered means trembled or shook convulsively.
